instruction: Determine each employee's age from their birthday, then calculate and record the average age in cell D30.

metadata.explanation: Task requires calculating ages for all 28 employees, then computing average and entering in D30. Comprehensive verification: (1) checks all 28 age cells are filled with numeric values, (2) spot-checks at least 5 employee ages are correctly calculated from birthdays, (3) verifies average in D30 is computed from the filled ages (not hardcoded), (4) confirms average equals expected 31.64 within tolerance 0.5. Custom getter reads all birthdays, ages, and average; metric validates all requirements.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator verifies ALL 4 instruction requirements comprehensively
Requirement 1 (calculate ages): Spot-checks at least 5 employee ages are correctly calculated from birthdays using current_year - birth_year with 1-year tolerance for birthday timing (lines 79-107)
Requirement 2 (fill ages): Verifies all 28 age cells are filled with numeric values (lines 76-77)
Requirement 3 (compute average): Verifies average in D30 is computed from filled ages by comparing D30 value to independently computed average, preventing hardcoded values (lines 113-122)
Requirement 4 (correct average): Verifies average matches expected 31.64 within tolerance 0.5 (lines 124-132)
Getter logic is correct: Reads birthdays (C2:C29), ages (D2:D29), average (D30), counts filled ages
Metric logic is robust: Handles edge cases (None values, non-datetime birthdays, non-numeric ages), uses appropriate tolerance for floating-point comparison
Anti-cheating: User cannot skip age calculations and just type '31.64' in D30 because metric verifies average is computed from actual age values (line 121 check)
